title: TARGET AND STATUS FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE UNDER PMAY-G
body_text:
Under Pradhan MantriAwaasYojana- Gramin, a total of 32.47 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 26.57 lakh houses have been completed during FY 2025 -26 , inclusive of sanctions issued in previous financial years. The State/UT-wise details are provided at Annexure - I.
A s on 03.08.2026, against the total target of 4.18 crore houses allocated to the States/UTs under PMAY-G, 3.91 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 3.12 crore houses have been completed. The remaining 79 lakh sanctioned houses are under construction.
Under PMAY-G, the house is constructed by the beneficiary himself/herself or under his/her supervision. Further, as per the guidelines of PMAY-G, the States/UTs provide the beneficiaries a bouquet of options of house designs according to the local climatic conditions, using appropriate local material and technology suitable to the region of their residence. The State/UT Government can also facilitate supply of construction material at competitive rates. The Ministry of Rural Development has published a compendium of rural housing typologies “PAHAL” which is available on the program website of PMAY-G. This can be accessed through AwaasApp. Further, to ensure good quality construction of houses under PMAY-G, the Government of India has rolled out Rural Mason Training (RMT) Program with the target to train adequate number of masons for house construction in rural areas.
A number of steps have been taken by the Ministry to ensure timely construction of houses in all States/UTs under PMAY-G. These include:
(i) Timely allocation of targets to the States/UTs and release of adequate funds;
(ii) Regular review of progress;
(iii) Monitoring and supervision of the scheme on a Dashboard;
(iv) Regular Workshops are conducted by the Ministry with the States/UTs;
(v) Rural Mason Training program, etc.
In addition to the unit assistance provided under the scheme, PMAY-G households are also provided with piped drinking water through convergence with the JalJeevan Mission (JJM) and HarGharNal Se Jal (HGNSJ) of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, or other similar schemes. In addition, beneficiaries are supported with electricity connections through relevant schemes implemented by the Ministry of Power, State Governments, or UT Administrations, and are provided Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections under the Pradhan MantriUjjwalaYojana (PMUY) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas or other relevant schemes.
As per the scheme guidelines, up to 5% of the targets under PMAY-G, are reserved for Special Projects. E.g. for Rehabilitation / relocation of families whose houses have been completely /substantially damaged on account of Natural hazards as categorized in the extant National Disaster Management Plan of National Disaster Management Authority - Flood, earthquake, fire, etc.
Further, under PMAY-G, a minimum 60% of the target at the national level is earmarked for both Scheduled Caste (SC)/Schedules Tribes (ST) households subject to availability of such eligible beneficiaries.
Additionally, under Pradhan MantriJanjatiAdivasiNyayaMahaAbhiyan (PM-JANMAN) of Ministry of Tribal Affairs, the provision providing pucca houses to the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG) households with basic amenities is one of the interventions being implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.
The funds under PMAY-G are allocated to States/UTs, with each State/UT treated as a single unit. The distribution of these funds among districts is undertaken by the respective State/UT Governments. Over the last two financial years, expenditure under Special Projects stood at ₹528.04 crore, while Aspirational Districts recorded spending of ₹17,281.58 crore, inclusive of both Central and State shares. Further, under PM-JANMAN, a Central share of ₹2,465.38 crore was released for PVTG beneficiaries during FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26, against which a total expenditure of ₹6,329.06 crore was incurred, comprising contributions from both the Centre and the States.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development reported that under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), 32.47 lakh houses were sanctioned and 26.57 lakh completed in FY 2025-26. Cumulatively, against a total target of 4.18 crore houses, 3.91 crore have been sanctioned and 3.12 crore completed as of 3 August 2026, with 79 lakh houses under construction. The Minister of State also detailed convergence with schemes like Jal Jeevan Mission, PMUY, and PM-JANMAN, and reservation norms for SC/ST households and Special Projects.
enrichment.context:
PMAY-G (launched 2016, restructured from the Indira Awaas Yojana) aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to eligible rural households, targeting the poorest based on Socio-Economic Caste Census deprivation criteria. It embodies the beneficiary-led construction model, where funds are directly transferred and houses built by beneficiaries themselves, unlike contractor-driven housing schemes, to ensure ownership and design flexibility (as seen in the 'PAHAL' typology compendium). The scheme's convergence approach—linking housing with water (Jal Jeevan Mission), electricity, and clean cooking fuel (Ujjwala)—reflects the government's push for holistic rural development and the 'Housing for All' vision.

The scheme also has an equity dimension: at least 60% of targets are reserved for SC/ST households, and special quotas exist for disaster-hit families and PVTGs under PM-JANMAN, a newer mission (2024) for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups. The mention of Aspirational Districts spending highlights continued focus on India's most underdeveloped districts, a NITI Aayog-led convergence initiative. Such periodic parliamentary replies are important trackers of scheme performance, inter-state disparities (e.g., high completion in Chhattisgarh vs stagnant sanctioning in states like Uttar Pradesh or West Bengal), and effectiveness of monitoring mechanisms like dashboards and mason training programs aimed at construction quality.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G):
1. Houses under PMAY-G are constructed directly by state government contractors.
2. A minimum of 60% of the national target is earmarked for SC/ST households.
3. Up to 5% of targets are reserved for Special Projects including disaster rehabilitation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, houses are constructed by the beneficiary or under their supervision, not by contractors, making statement 1 incorrect. Statements 2 and 3 are directly confirmed by the release regarding SC/ST reservation and Special Projects reservation.

prelims_questions.question: The 'PAHAL' compendium mentioned in connection with PMAY-G relates to which of the following?
options: A digital payment platform for beneficiaries
A compendium of rural housing typologies and designs
A skill certification program for rural masons
A grievance redressal mechanism for housing complaints
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the Ministry of Rural Development has published PAHAL as a compendium of rural housing typologies, accessible via the program website and AwaasApp, to help beneficiaries choose designs suited to local conditions.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the beneficiary-led construction model under PMAY-G in achieving the goal of 'Housing for All' in rural India. Examine the challenges in ensuring quality construction and timely completion of targets.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance: Welfare Schemes for Vulnerable Sections

mains_questions.question: Convergence of housing schemes with water, electricity, and LPG connectivity is central to holistic rural development. Critically evaluate the effectiveness of such inter-ministerial convergence mechanisms using PMAY-G as a case study.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions for Development

related_articles.relationship: PMAY-Urban is the urban counterpart scheme to PMAY-Gramin, both being housing-for-all missions, and this release similarly reports sanctioning and completion milestones for the same overarching PMAY program.
